question: Neonatal hypoglycaemia is defined as a blood glucose level below 45 mg/dL, and this threshold applies regardless of the gestational age or postnatal age of the neonate.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The statement is TRUE. Neonatal hypoglycaemia = blood glucose <45 mg/dL. This is the standard clinical threshold used in Indian and international paediatric practice. Gestational age affects the RISK of hypoglycaemia, not the threshold. At-risk groups (IDM, SGA/IUGR, preterm, LGA) need earlier and more frequent screening, but the treatment threshold remains <45 mg/dL.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! The operational clinical threshold for neonatal hypoglycaemia is blood glucose <45 mg/dL (IAP/AAP guidelines). This threshold applies to all neonates — term, preterm, SGA, IDM — and at any postnatal age during the neonatal period. The physiological nadir in the first 1–2 hours may transiently fall to 40–50 mg/dL but should recover; any glucose <45 mg/dL with symptoms, or persistently <40 mg/dL even without symptoms in at-risk groups, warrants treatment.
